name: Ouagadougou
subtitle: Ouagadougou, capital of Burkina Faso: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 2,415,266 people live in the commune of Ouagadougou (counted 2019).
The commune of Ouagadougou covers 518 km2, or 0.2 per cent of the national territory.
Ouagadougou's 2019 population is 11.78 per cent of Burkina Faso's total and 45.1 per cent of its urban population.

parts.text: The commune of Ouagadougou covers 518 km2, or 0.2 per cent of the national territory.
Ouagadougou's 2019 population is 11.78 per cent of Burkina Faso's total and 45.1 per cent of its urban population.
The commune population rose from 441,514 in 1985 to 1,475,839 in 2006 and 2,415,266 in 2019.
The commune lies on a vast peneplain of the Centre region with altitudes between 300 and 350 m.
The rainy season lasts from June to September and concentrates nearly 80 per cent of the rain.
As capital of the state and seat of region, province and department, Ouagadougou hosts the headquarters of all ministries.
Mooré is the dominant language among the main languages commonly spoken in the commune of Ouagadougou.
Population density in the commune rose from 2,847.9 inhabitants per km2 in 2006 to 4,385.5 in 2019.
The short rainy season feeds four dams inside the city, used for drinking water, market gardening and fishing.
Ouagadougou is also the capital of the largest and strongest Mossi kingdom of the same name.
The ruler of the Ouagadougou kingdom bore the title Mogho (or Moro) Naba, meaning "ruler of the world".

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in the commune of Ouagadougou?

parts.text: 2,415,266 in 2019, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Commune of Ouagadougou (518 km2), 5th General Census of Population and Housing (RGPH 2019); 1,183,557 men and 1,231,709 women.

items.text: The Voulet mission entered Ouagadougou, capital of the Mossi empire, and signed a treaty of peace and protectorate with the Mossi naba on 20 January 1897.
The decree of 1 March 1919 created the colony of Haute-Volta by dividing Haut-Sénégal-Niger.
The first stone of the palace of the Baloum Naaba, official spokesman of the Mogho Naaba, was laid on 22 November 1922.
Haute-Volta was re-established by law no. 47-1707 of 4 September 1947.
The central market left the site of the present Place de la Révolution in 1954 and moved to its current 3.6 ha site, Rood-woko.
On 26 August 1985 the reconstruction of the central market was decided as part of the planning scheme for the commercial zone.
The mixed-economy company SOGEMA-B, which manages the new central market Rood-woko, was created on 9 March 1988 for 99 years.
A fire swept through the central market in 2003, after which the city authorities took strict measures.
The 2019 census counted 2,415,266 inhabitants in the commune.
